analysis: The only change in this file is a single line in acquireResliceGate() at head line 305, which adds `resliceGateGeneration &+= 1` after `isReslicing = true` (patch hunk @@ -302,6 +302,7 @@). It is a wrapping increment of a counter on the ProviderLoop actor. No trust boundary, crypto, authorization, attestation or data-exposure code is touched. The surrounding base text covers re-slice orchestration: the KV grant shrink/build/restore sequence, the serviceability floor, and the weight-release ordering. It also covers the registration of the bridge with engineV2Runtime. None of that logic is modified. I found no impact on T-041 (SSD prefix cache), which only lists this file as affected; its cache construction is delegated to EngineV2SlotFactory and is unchanged. Wrapping arithmetic (&+=) cannot trap, so there is no new availability risk from overflow. Open question for integration: the declaration of `resliceGateGeneration` and its consumers are not in the supplied units. Integration should confirm it is declared in ProviderLoop.swift and is only used as a gate/staleness token, for example to detect that a held gate was released and reacquired. It should not feed any security decision such as authorization or grant binding. Since the declaration and readers are outside the supplied evidence, I cannot verify those uses, but nothing here suggests a regression.
